title: Mechanical Model: Chassis, Tracks and Terrain

blocks.text: This chapter describes the STRUCTURE domain of the digital twin: the chassis rigid body, the two rubber tracks, the contact between track and terrain, and the worlds the robot drives in. Together these parts turn the sprocket torques of the drive train into vehicle motion. They also produce the true vehicle state that the sensor models, the monitors and the test oracles read. In the model they live in `structure_plant`, which `Shaddad_Plant` instantiates as the Subsystem Reference block `Structure`. `scripts/build/build_structure.m` (and `scripts/build/build_structure_env.m` for `structure_env`) generate the files from the parameters in `params/param_structure.m` and `params/param_world.m`. The design is documented in `docs/specs/structure.md` (revision B) and in decisions D36, D39, D40, D53 and D62 of `docs/architecture.md`.
Role in the Digital Twin

Shaddad is a tracked skid-steer platform. It steers by driving its left and right tracks at different speeds, so the track-terrain model decides how well the robot follows the operator's speed and yaw-rate commands. In Phase 1 the MCU converts the RC speed and yaw-rate request into two track-speed references. The ESCs drive the PMSMs, and the 24:1 gearboxes turn the two sprockets. `structure_plant` receives those sprocket shafts as Simscape rotational ports. It returns the motion of the robot on the selected terrain, the reaction torques on the sprockets and the load of the active implement. {fig:F12_structure_plant.png} shows the domain top level. {tab:tab_struct_ports} lists its interface.

blocks.text: {tab:tab_struct_files} lists the model files. Helper functions: `structure_contact_normal.m` and `structure_planar_forces.m` (bodies of the two MATLAB Function blocks), `utilities/structure_initial_state.m` (settled start pose), `utilities/structure_mass_properties.m` (independent mass-property check) and `utilities/structure_identify_chi.m` (steering-factor identification).

Do not edit the generated .slx files by hand. Change the build script, the helper or the parameter file, then run `build_structure` (all files except `structure_env`) or `build_structure({'structure_contact'})` (one file). `structure_env` is rebuilt with `build_structure_env`. The builds are idempotent. The MATLAB Function blocks carry verbatim copies of `structure_contact_normal.m` and `structure_planar_forces.m`, so after editing a helper you must rebuild `structure_contact`. The test `t_structure/mf_bodies_current` detects a stale copy.
Frames and Sign Conventions

items: **Reference point R**: at ground level (undeformed track bottom), midway between the track centrelines and at mid contact length. All component positions in `P.structure` are body FRD coordinates relative to R, so z < 0 means above ground.
**Internal integration**: the 6DOF block integrates the CG in flat-Earth NED with a body FRD frame and ZYX Euler angles (Aerospace Blockset convention).

**Domain boundary**: `structure_truth` converts everything to the world frame W = site ENU at `P.world.lla0` = [24.1556 N, 47.3120 E, 430 m] (Al-Kharj palm district) and to the body frame B = FLU: `R_WB = R_NED_ENU' * DCM_be' * R_FRD_FLU`.
`pose2D` = [x_E, y_N, psi], with psi measured counter-clockwise from East (the GNC convention). `omega_B(3) > 0` is a left turn. `eul(2) > 0` is nose down, so a climb shows a negative pitch.
Track index 1 = left, 2 = right. Positive sprocket rotation means forward track motion on both sides; the drive domain handles the motor mirroring.
Contact forces act on the vehicle: F_x > 0 pushes the robot forward, and the belt receives -F_x.

blocks.text: Chassis Rigid Body

The chassis is the Aerospace Blockset block `Simple Variable Mass 6DOF (Euler Angles)` (library `aerolib6dof2`) in `structure_body6dof`. With `mass_flag` on, the block exposes mass and inertia to the separate `6DOF Acceleration` and `6DOF Angular Acceleration` blocks. A full 6DOF body was chosen because heave, roll and pitch then follow from the compliant terrain contact, so slope attitude, load transfer and the IMU specific force are physical. Simscape Multibody is not installed, the robotmobilelib models are kinematic only, and the Aerospace 3DOF block works only in the x-z plane, so none of these was suitable.

m (dv_b/dt + omega x v_b) = F_b
J domega/dt + omega x (J omega) + dJ/dt omega = M_b
F_b = m C_bn [0 0 g]' + sum_j F_c,j + F_impl + F_ext
M_b = sum_j r_j x F_c,j + r_impl x F_impl + M_impl + M_ext
g = 9.7876 m/s^2 (P.frames.g, WGS-84 gravity at 430 m, 24.15 N)

Variable mass matters only with the sprayer: the tank outflow enters the `dm/dt` input, and the block interpolates the inertia between the empty and full tensors. The 6DOF block assumes a CG fixed in the body. The model therefore applies the tank-induced CG shift to the contact lever arms through `r_cg(m) = (m_e r_cg,e + (m - m_e) r_tank)/m`, which is exact for the forces. Without a sprayer, `mass_f = mass_e + 1e-3 kg` and dm/dt = 0. {tab:tab_struct_mass} gives the mass breakdown. {tab:tab_struct_mp} gives the resulting mass properties.

blocks.text: `param_structure` calls `structure_initial_state`, which solves the static equilibrium of the 14 contact springs for heave, pitch and roll at `P.world.start` by Newton iteration. A run therefore starts settled, with no drop transient. On flat asphalt the settled base robot pitches 0.167° nose up because its CG lies 22 mm behind R. The simulated value matches the analytic one.
Track Model

Each side has an 11-tooth sprocket (72 mm pitch, r_s = 0.128 m), an idler, five road wheels and a 180 mm rubber belt with a 1.0 m ground contact length. The track gauge is B = 0.85 m (L/B = 1.18). The model has three parts: a Simscape sprocket/belt network per side, 14 compliant contact points, and a two-dimensional shear law that turns belt-over-ground slip into traction and side force.
Sprocket and Belt Network

`structure_track_side` is a Simscape network in the classic foundation rotational and translational domains, the same domain as the drive gearbox outputs. The chain runs from port `Spr` through an Ideal Torque Sensor to the Inertia `J_eq`, which represents the sprocket, idler and road wheels. A Rotational Friction element connects `J_eq` to the chassis reference and models the internal track loss. A Wheel and Axle block (radius r_s) links the sprocket to the belt Mass, and an Ideal Force Source applies the ground shear force -F_x to the belt. Motion and torque sensors output the belt speed, the sprocket angle, speed and torque, and the friction power.

J_eq domega_s/dt = T_spr - T_fric(omega_s) - r_s F_axle
m_belt dv_b/dt  = F_axle - F_x ,          v_b = r_s omega_s
T_fric: Coulomb T_col = f_c N_nom r_s (f_c = 0.015), breakaway 1.3 T_col at 0.05 rad/s,
        viscous c_visc = 0.005 N_nom r_s^2,   N_nom = m0 g / 2 (static load per track)
For the base robot N_nom = 2296 N, which gives T_col = 4.4 N m per side. The reflected motor inertia and the gearbox output inertia belong to the drive domain and are not repeated here.
Contact Points and Normal Force

Each track has 7 segment-centred contact points at x = 0, ±0.143, ±0.286 and ±0.429 m, y = -0.425 m (left, points 1-7) or +0.425 m (right, points 8-14), z = 0 relative to R (`P.structure.contact.Rc_R`). `structure_contact` computes the point positions and velocities from the 6DOF states. Eight 2-D Lookup Tables on `P.world` (linear interpolation, clipped, evenly spaced index search) then give the terrain height, the two gradients and five soil properties at every point. MF-A (`structure_contact_normal.m`) evaluates a compliant spring-damper law:

n_z   = 1 / sqrt(1 + hE^2 + hN^2)
pen_j = (D_j + h_j) n_z                         (> 0 = below the surface)
N_j   = [pen_j > 0] max(0, kc kScale_j pen_j + cc sqrt(kScale_j) dpen_j/dt)
kc = 3.2e4 N/m and cc = 1.0e3 N s/m per point

On hard ground the static deflection of the base robot is 10.25 mm; on soft soil it grows by 1/kScale. The mean ground pressure is 12.8 kPa at 469.2 kg and 16.6 kPa at 609.2 kg. MF-B applies the normal force along the local terrain normal rather than along the body z axis. This T03 refinement of the spec removes a spurious N sin(pitch) force caused by the compliance pitch. Every contact input comes from a state (6DOF, integrators, Simscape belt speed), so the contact model creates no algebraic loop.
Two-Dimensional Shear and Slip

Decision D39 gives each of the 14 points an isotropic 2-D shear state s_j = [s_x; s_y]. These 28 Integrator states sit in `structure_track_shear` and are limited to ±1. They are driven by the resultant slip velocity of the belt over the ground. MF-B (`structure_planar_forces.m`) evaluates the law per point:

v_slip,j = [v_b,i - v_x,j ; -v_y,j]                         belt minus ground, body axes
ds_j/dt  = (v_slip,j - |v_slip,j| s_j)/K_j - (|v_b,i|/l) s_j     l = L/2 = 0.5 m
mu_j     = mu_p mu_lat |s_j| / sqrt((mu_lat s_x)^2 + (mu_p s_y)^2)   friction ellipse
F_j      = sat( mu_j N_j [g(|s_j|) s_j/|s_j| + tau_d ds_j/dt] , mu_j N_j )   tau_d = 0.01 s
g(s)     = f(2s/(1-s)),  f(x) = 1 - (1 - exp(-x))/x              lumped Janosi-Hanamoto
F_rr,j   = -f_r N_j tanh(v_x,j / 0.05)                         rolling resistance (body only)
F_x,i    = sum of F_x,j over track i  -> belt force source of track i

items: **Straight running**: the steady state reproduces the lumped Janosi-Hanamoto drawbar curve `F = mu_p N [1 - K/(iL) (1 - exp(-iL/K))]` exactly, with slip i = (v_b - v_g)/v_b.
**Standstill**: ds/dt = 0, so the state holds. A parked robot on a 20° slope has zero creep and only an elastic deflection.

**Numerics**: there is no slip-ratio division and no epsilon regularisation. The eigenvalue is at most about -400 1/s, which is stable with ode3 at 1 ms. The domain needs a step of 2 ms or less (`P.structure.sim.h_max`).
**Turning**: the lateral point velocities enlarge |v_slip|, so the isotropic law forces longitudinal slip, as in Wong's theory of skid steering.
**Loop breaker**: MF-B evaluates the shear law with the belt speed delayed by one 1 ms sample (`P.structure.track.vb_delay`, D36).

blocks.text: The truth and track buses report the slip as `slip = (v_belt - v_ground)/max(|v_belt|, 0.05)` per track. It is positive when the belt runs faster than the ground (driving) and negative when the track brakes.
Skid-Steer Turning and the Steering Factor chi

A skid-steer vehicle can only turn if its tracks slide sideways over the ground. Its yaw rate is therefore lower than the kinematic value (v_R - v_L)/B. The model expresses this with the effective gauge factor:

chi_eff = (v_bR - v_bL) / (B r)      r = yaw rate (FLU, + = left)
chi_eff = NaN while |r| < 0.05 rad/s (P.structure.track.chi_rmin)

chi = 1 describes an ideal differential drive. A larger chi means that a larger track-speed difference is needed for the same yaw rate. The turning-resistance moment `M_turn = sum_j x_j F_y,j` follows from the point model itself; the model does not add Wong's empirical radius correction mu_t(R/B). `structure_identify_chi` runs the HiFi bench on world 6 (soil_strips) with open-loop belt speeds: spot turns at ±0.5 m/s and steady R = 2 m turns at 0.5 m/s, repeated three times (option 'Iter') with the measured chi so that the radius approaches 2 m. It writes the results into `params/param_structure.m` ({tab:tab_struct_chi}). The farm-soil value `P.structure.track.chi_nom` = 1.3361 is the single source for the MCU track-speed mixer (`P.electronics.mix.chi`), the EKF prior (`P.sensors.ekf.chi0`), the LoFi chassis (`P.structure.lofi.chi`) and the GNC command envelope.

blocks.text: Test T10 checks the HiFi turn against an independent implementation of Wong's general theory of skid steering (`structure_analytic_refs('wong_turn', ...)`). The HiFi model gives chi_eff = 1.335 at R = 1.946 m and 0.484 m/s, against 1.243 from Wong (+7.4 %, criterion ±10 %). The sprocket torques are -47.3 N m inner and 98.8 N m outer, against -46.7 and 98.0 N m, and the turning power is 362 W against 348 W. As the theory predicts, the inner track brakes and the outer track drives. The identified values span 1.28-1.42. The farm-soil value 1.336 and the soft-soil values lie in the 1.3-1.8 range reported for tracked skid-steer vehicles; the hard greenhouse and asphalt surfaces give slightly lower values (1.28). The retired revision-A law gave only 1.01-1.08 (D39).

chi is identified from the HiFi model and mu_lat is an estimated soil parameter. Neither has been measured on the real robot (risk R14). They must be re-identified from field turning tests once the hardware exists [TBD - field turning tests after hardware bring-up]. Running `structure_identify_chi()` with the default 'Write' true rewrites the chi lines in `params/param_structure.m`. This changes the MCU mixer, the EKF prior, the LoFi chassis and the GNC limits, so rerun the affected tests afterwards.
Soil Types

Five soil classes are defined in `P.world.soilTable` ({tab:tab_struct_soil}). mu_p is the peak traction coefficient (Wong-based, c/p + tan phi), K is the shear deformation modulus, mu_lat is the lateral friction coefficient, f_r is the rolling-resistance coefficient, and kScale scales the contact stiffness, so softer soil sinks further. At constant speed on flat ground the steady slip satisfies f(iL/K) = f_r/mu_p, so it does not depend on the mass. The last column gives the slip that the HiFi model reaches at 1 m/s in test T4.

blocks.caption: Soil classes (P.world.soilTable) and steady straight-line slip at 1 m/s (T03 test T4)

blocks.text: Each world stores an integer soil class grid `soilId` and five property grids. For worlds 3-6, `world_build` blends the property grids over one 0.25 m cell (3 x 3 box filter), so the soil changes smoothly as a track crosses from one class to another. In the procedural worlds 1-2 only the linear lookup interpolation smooths a soil boundary, over one cell. The scenario input `env_ovr` (`use_soil`, `soil_id`) forces one class on all 14 points; the bench tests use it (T2, T4, T5, T9, T10, T18). `structure_identify_chi` instead drives on the soil strips of world 6. `Bus_EnvState.soil_id` reports the class under R.
Terrain and World Model

`P.world` is the single world description shared by STRUCTURE (contact), SENSORS (LiDAR, GNSS sky view), GNC (a-priori map) and Sim_Monitors (collision). `param_world(worldId, g)` generates worlds 1 and 2 procedurally and calls `utilities/world_build.m` for worlds 3-6, whose geometry is defined in `world_scn_<name>.m` ({tab:tab_struct_worlds}). Random draws come only from a fixed seed (20261026), so each world can be reproduced exactly. Every world contains:

items: a DEM `H` with gradients `dHdE` and `dHdN` on a 0.25 m grid (`Table(i,j)` belongs to `(xE(i), yN(j))`), plus soil, vegetation-density and shade grids
obstacles: cylinders (palm trunks, posts, solar piers) and boxes (walls, test boxes, solar tables), canopy circles and greenhouse film segments
GNSS sky-view and zone grids, lane centrelines (`rows`), a geofence (`boundary`), start and dock poses, and a 10 cells/m occupancy grid

blocks.text: Worlds 3-5 correspond to the three environments in which NASL offers Shaddad services: palm farms, greenhouses and solar farms. The greenhouse world uses the standard 360 m² house that NASL quotes for its greenhouse coverage figure. `P.world.env` sets the design climate: T_amb = 318.15 K (45 °C), G_solar = 1000 W/m² under open sky (scaled by the shade grid, 0.6 in the greenhouse and 0.2 under the panels), the ground up to 15 K above ambient (scaled by G_solar/1000) and the sky 12 K below. `structure_env` publishes these values in `Bus_EnvState` every 0.1 s. It is the single source of T_amb for the power, drive, electronics and sensor models.

Obstacles exert no contact forces. Collision handling is detection only: Sim_Monitors checks the robot footprint against the nearest cylinders and boxes (D42) and reports `collision` and `clear_min` in `Bus_SimKPI`. If the robot leaves the DEM, the lookups clip (the terrain continues flat) and `diag.outOfMap` becomes true; Sim_Monitors copies it to `Bus_SimKPI.out_of_map`. No test asserts it yet, so check it after runs on custom worlds.
Implement Mechanics

`structure_implement` selects the attachment with `VC_IMPL`: 0 none, 1 mower, 2 tiller, 3 sprayer. These are the three Shaddad attachments. Each choice is a rotational load on `Impl_Shaft`. The mower and tiller also apply a force on the chassis at the tool (the mower yaw moment k_yaw T_cut is present but k_yaw = 0). The sprayer applies no chassis force; it feeds dm/dt to the 6DOF block, so its mass and CG change. {tab:tab_struct_impl} summarises the load models. In the system (`VC_IMPL_DRIVE = 2`) the implement motor in Power_Plant drives the shaft. `VC_IMPL_DRIVE = 1`, an ideal speed source, is used only on the bench. All load torques use the shaft speed delayed by 1 ms (D36), and `impl_mech` leaves the plant at 0.01 s (D32). The Phase 1 demonstration in this report runs with `VC_IMPL = 0`.

blocks.text: Truth Outputs

`structure_truth` converts the internal NED/FRD state at the CG into quantities at the reference point R, in ENU/FLU, and assembles `Bus_TruthState` ({tab:tab_struct_truth}). `Shaddad_Plant` exports the bus at 1 ms. The IMU, GNSS, encoder and LiDAR models, Sim_Monitors and the logging read it. The controllers never use it: they see only the simulated sensors.

blocks.text: `Bus_TrackState` carries per track `v_belt`, `v_ground`, `slip`, `s_shear`, `Fx`, `Fy`, `Fn`, `sprAngle`, `sprSpeed`, `sprTorque`, `sinkage`, `muPeak`, `Mturn` and `Pslip`. `Bus_StructureDiag` carries the 14 point values `N_pt`, `pen_pt`, `sX` and `sY`, together with `slopeLong`, `slopeLat`, `P_diss`, `E_mech`, `E_diss_J`, `E_impl_shaft_J`, `chi_eff` and `outOfMap`. The energy terms feed the mechanical energy audit `eps_mech = |sum(E_spr) - E_diss - dE_mech| / sum(E_spr)` (D40). In the S1 RC drive this residual is 4.4e-5: the structure plant accounts for the sprocket energy to within 0.005 %. A system run logs `truth` (decimation 10, so 10 ms samples), `struct_diag` (0.01 s) and `env` (0.1 s). Runs longer than 600 s log every signal at 0.1 s (`P.log.Ts_mission`).
Structure Signals in the Phase 1 Demonstration

The D1 demo drive (`phase1_test_drive`, world 1 flat_test, HiFi chassis, no implement) covers 34.8 m without a collision. In every segment the speed and yaw rate follow the commands to within 0.025 m/s and 0.011 rad/s. {fig:F31_drive_internals.png} shows the drive internals of this run. The belt-slip panel plots `truth.slip_LR`. Read it as follows: in steady straight driving on farm soil the slip should stay near the analytic 0.57 % at 1 m/s (T4). In a moving arc the outer track drives and the inner track brakes (T10). In the pivot turn both tracks slip strongly in their direction of belt motion (T9: about 28 % at ±0.5 m/s).

blocks.text: Test T18 compares the two variants on a palm_farm course: 100 m straight at 1 m/s, then a 180° right turn with R = 4 m at 0.5 m/s, on farm soil with open-loop sprocket speeds. The end positions differ by 0.132 m (HiFi [15.95, 108.63] m, LoFi [15.97, 108.50] m; heading difference 3.56°), and the sprocket energies by 1.5 % (51.6 kJ against 52.4 kJ). With a closed yaw-rate PI loop like the MCU's (T18b, Kp 0.4, Ki 2.0) the heading difference falls to 0.14°. LoFi is adequate for planar mission questions. It shows only quasi-static attitude, track loads and sinkage from the DEM and the soil grid at R. It cannot show heave, pitch or roll dynamics, contact compliance, per-point load distribution, soil-dependent slip or slip dynamics.

To use LoFi in a system run, assign `VC_STRUCT_FID = 2` in the base workspace before calling `run_scenario`. `scn_base_input` copies every base-workspace `VC_*` value into the run unless the scenario sets it itself. LoFi has not been exercised in the Phase 1 system scenarios; it is verified on the structure bench only.
Verification (Build Task T03)

`tests/structure/t_structure.m` has 20 tests. In the system acceptance regression 19 passed and 1 failed (T19 LoFi speed). The tests drive the bench `tests/structure/tb_structure.slx` with ideal sprocket speed or torque sources and compare the results with the analytic references in `tests/structure/structure_analytic_refs.m`. {tab:tab_struct_t03} lists the measured values from the T03 test log.

blocks.text: **Turning on slopes (T7b).** The D53 design review expected a 609 kg robot to slide downhill in an R = 2 m turn on a 20° slope, because the outer track would need about 1950 N against 1850 N available. The HiFi model reaches 87 % traction utilisation at 20° (74 % at 15°) and does not slide at the traction limit. Without position control, however, the turn centre creeps downhill by about 1.15 m (15°) and 1.6 m (20°) per full turn because of shear relaxation and the asymmetry between uphill and downhill slip. The D53 slope rules therefore stay in force: the GNC limits the yaw rate with tilt, inhibits pivot turns above 10° and places no headland turns where the slope exceeds 10°.

**Slope attitude (T16).** On the 20° ramp the chassis sits 0.024 rad steeper than the rigid-body value, because the 14 contact springs compress more at the downhill end. The truth bus and the IMU model include this compliance pitch. It is listed in `docs/STATUS.md` as an accepted spec deviation.

blocks.text: Working with the Structure Model

Every command below needs the project to be open; opening it runs `shaddad_startup`, which creates `P`, `Ts`, the `VC_*` variables and the bus objects. Run everything in Normal mode, because Accelerator MEX files are blocked by Windows Application Control on this PC.

items: **Choose a world and an implement for a Phase 1 drive.** `phase1_test_drive` accepts 'World' and 'Implement'. The example drives straight along the dry-sand strip of world 6, which starts at [-5 5 0].
**Read the structure signals from a result.** Every run returns the logged signals in `res.S`.
**Run the structure bench on its own.** The bench is faster than the full system and shows the track and contact buses directly.
**Run the tests, inspect a world, rebuild a file.**

blocks.text:
% 4) tests, worlds, rebuild
runtests('t_structure', 'Tag', 'Data')        % T1 mass properties, analytic references (seconds)
runtests('t_structure/T9_spot_turn')          % one bench test
res = structure_identify_chi('Write', false);  % re-identify chi without changing the parameter file
W = param_world(3);  world_plot(W);           % terrain, soil, sky view, occupancy of palm_farm
build_structure({'structure_contact'})        % rebuild one file after editing a helper

The full `t_structure` suite takes about 40 minutes. Use the tags 'Data', 'Bench', 'Perf' and 'Build' to run parts of it. The bench runner `structure_tb_run` passes P, Ts and the VC_* values through `Simulink.SimulationInput`, so it never changes the shared base workspace.
Limitations and Open Points

items: Collisions are detected but produce no impact forces. Tank slosh, implement compliance, track tension and derailment are not modelled.
Wong's radius-dependent turning resistance is not added. chi and mu_lat are not yet validated against field data [TBD - field turning tests, risk R14].
The contact compliance adds 0.024 rad of pitch on a 20° slope. The truth state includes it (accepted deviation).
The enclosure thermal node and the obstacle monitor described in the structure spec are not part of `structure_plant`. Collision checking is done in Sim_Monitors.

Reference-solver mode (`run_scenario(..., 'Solver', 'ref')`) fails. One cause is in this domain: `structure_hifi/StructureDiag` mixes continuous and 0.001 s signals in a nonvirtual Bus Creator (STATUS open problem 12).
LoFi reaches RTF 67.5 against a target of 100. Accelerator mode is currently blocked on this PC, so all runs use Normal mode.
Outside the DEM the terrain continues flat (`outOfMap` flag).
